facts.statement: The study investigated whether personal differences in achievement goals change brain activity in the ventral striatum when people receive negative feedback.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants performed a word association task and got feedback on their performance while their brains were scanned using fMRI.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Brain reactions to negative feedback were linked to how strongly participants focused on approaching goals.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People with stronger approach goals showed a smaller drop in ventral striatum activity in response to negative feedback compared to the usual pattern.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The findings suggest that personal achievement goals can work with the situation to shape how negative feedback is perceived.
facts.subject: humans
